question: Identify the single cell organism.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amoeba** is a single-celled organism commonly found in freshwater environments.
 
• It belongs to the **protist kingdom** and is known for its ability to change shape due to its flexible cell membrane.
 
• Amoebas move by extending their **pseudopodia** (false feet), which are temporary projections of the cell.
 
• They feed through a process called **phagocytosis**, where they engulf food particles with their pseudopodia.
 
• Amoebas reproduce asexually through a process called **binary fission**, where the cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seaweed**

 
 
• Seaweeds are multicellular marine algae and are not single-celled organisms.
 
• They play a crucial role in marine ecosystems, providing food and habitat for marine life.
 
 
 
• **Leech**
 
 
• Leeches are multicellular parasitic or predatory worms belonging to the phylum Annelida.
 
• They are known for their bloodsucking behavior and are used in medical treatments for bloodletting.
 
 
 
• **Liver fluke**
 
 
• Liver flukes are parasitic flatworms belonging to the class Trematoda.
 
• They infect the liver and bile ducts of various mammals, including humans.
